- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +10–15% of spike peak.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion bias toward prior 5–10 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; smooth out extremes by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ days, model often drifts toward overestimation; apply downward bias of 1–2% per day.
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often ignores trend; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment decay.
